about.title: Riverside Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Riverside sits where SR-91 and I-215 come together, and a large share of the city's daily traffic moves along those two freeways or down Van Buren Boulevard toward the airport, March Field and the neighborhoods in between. In 2025, public records show 1,995 injury collisions inside city limits, with 2,807 people hurt and 23 traffic deaths. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. carry the highest concentration of reported crashes. If one of those collisions involved you, the weeks that follow can feel scattered: a damaged car, calls from an adjuster, appointments you never planned for. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Riverside residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency. You pay nothing for the introduction, and the attorney earns a fee only if your claim produces a recovery. In the meantime, keep your photos, medical paperwork and the other driver's details somewhere safe.

items.title: The clock in California is shorter than people expect
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but a claim against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. An early connection with an attorney helps protect those deadlines.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than wiped out. Attorneys in our network know how to push back when an insurer inflates your percentage.

items.title: Contingency fees and no cap on non-economic damages
items.desc: California places no statutory cap on pain-and-suffering damages in ordinary car accident cases, and network attorneys charge nothing unless there is a recovery. That structure lets you pursue the full claim without paying up front.

items.question: My crash happened on I-215 or SR-91 in Riverside. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. Freeway collisions sometimes involve questions about road design, signage, work zones or maintenance, and if a public agency such as Caltrans is potentially responsible, California requires a government claim within roughly six months instead of the usual two years. An attorney can evaluate whether that shorter window applies to your situation. Because several agencies share responsibility for Riverside roads, sorting that out early matters.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and doing so before you understand your injuries can work against you. Adjusters may use casual phrasing or an early estimate of how you feel to minimize your claim later. It is reasonable to decline politely and let an attorney handle communications. Your own insurer may have cooperation requirements, so review your policy separately.

items.question: What should I keep after a Riverside car accident to support my claim?
items.answer: Hold on to photos of the vehicles, the roadway and any visible injuries, along with the police report number, the other driver's insurance information and every medical record and receipt. If a nearby business or home may have camera footage, note the location quickly since recordings are often overwritten within days. Write down your own account while it is fresh. Preserving these details gives an attorney far more to work with when reconstructing what happened.
